questions.passage:
Cooler Streets
On hot afternoons, pavement stores heat and releases it slowly. Shade trees can reduce the sunlight reaching a sidewalk. Water evaporating from leaves can also cool the surrounding air. These benefits vary with tree size, species, water supply, and location.
A neighborhood group measured sidewalk temperatures at noon on three clear days. The shaded site averaged 29°C; the unshaded site averaged 36°C. Both sites had the same paving material. The group recommended planting trees along a busy walking route.
The measurements support a local cooling benefit, but they do not prove that every tree will lower every sidewalk temperature by seven degrees. Underground utilities and limited planting space also matter. A useful plan combines measurements with information about each location.

questions.passage:
Cooler Streets
On hot afternoons, pavement stores heat and releases it slowly. Shade trees can reduce the sunlight reaching a sidewalk. Water evaporating from leaves can also cool the surrounding air. These benefits vary with tree size, species, water supply, and location.
A neighborhood group measured sidewalk temperatures at noon on three clear days. The shaded site averaged 29°C; the unshaded site averaged 36°C. Both sites had the same paving material. The group recommended planting trees along a busy walking route.
The measurements support a local cooling benefit, but they do not prove that every tree will lower every sidewalk temperature by seven degrees. Underground utilities and limited planting space also matter. A useful plan combines measurements with information about each location.

After the Storm
The street wore mirrors after rain;
each puddle held a piece of sky.
A bus swept through the silver lane,
and scattered clouds went racing by.
I stopped beside one quiet pool:

Two Views of the Library's Empty Room
Text A — Student letter: Our library should use its empty room for quiet study. Last month I could not find a quiet seat on four afternoons. Students need somewhere to concentrate after school. A study room could open immediately with the tables we already own.
Text B — Librarian's proposal: The empty room should become a workshop. A survey of 80 visitors found that 52 wanted classes in repairing household items. We could offer quiet study there when classes are not running. Workshops would require supplies and a volunteer coordinator, so we should test the plan for one month before making it permanent.
